title: Purpose
text:
The open data actions and measures toolkit provides guidance on how to measure organizational actions and public engagement with open data to present a cohesive view of the activity and use of open data in a community. The actions and measures shared in the toolkit were identified from case study research of 3 local governments in the U.S. and from a literature review on open data use, participation, engagement, and user-friendly data products.
The examples provided in the toolkit represent the data portals, products, and measures from organizations who participated in the case study research of the City of Austin, the City of Baton Rouge and Parish of East Baton Rouge, and the City and County of San Francisco.

Measures
Common ways that people use open data is by viewing a dataset, map, dashboard, visualization, news article, or an application. Measures of these types of activities are called page views or view counts.
Downloads of data and requests to API (application programming interface) endpoints for datasets are other ways that the public use open data, often with analysis and coding tools that ease the connection to data and enable automatic refreshes.
Learn how to access web analytics from open data portal platforms.


Actions
Actions include the creation of data products (new data, maps, applications, dashboards, narrative, visualizations, articles) and enablement acts (support, communications, events, community coordination, promotion) by open data programs and other members of the community to empower the public to use open data meaningfully.
View types of actions that demonstrate intent to enable and empower the public.


Engagement
Other signals of open data activity in the community include attendance at events, views of tutorials, knowledge base articles, and videos, communications, support requests, public information requests, and council and organization mandates for new data.
View ways of tracking engagement with open data by the public, intermediaries, and community advocates.


Reporting
Reporting is an important way to link organizational actions with measures of success. Annual reports, performance dashboards, and blog posts provide opportunities to explain why an action is important.
View recommendations for reporting contents and cadence as well as examples by programs and community organizations.

title: Web Analytics
text: The first step to find analytic information is to locate the data catalog on a data portal. Organizations may have multiple data portals that house their data. Common data portal providers that publish web analytic information include Tyler Technologies1 and Esri2.

title: Web Analytics
text:
Web Analytics
Data portals publish the number of page views for data assets on overview pages and through APIs (application programming interface).

Overview Pages
Dataset overview pages provide important details about the data and lifetime page views and downloads. An example of an overview page is the Issued Construction Permits on the Austin data portal.



Issued Building Permits


In the “About” section, the lifetime views and downloads are shown, which for this dataset consist of 5.38 million views and 82.3 thousand downloads.


APIs (Application programming interfaces)
The Tyler Technologies Discovery API3 provides analytic details for all data assets on a data portal that includes lifetime views and downloads, as well as views in the last week and month, providing insights on current public interest. Authentication is not required to access information about published data assets on domain. Tools like Excel and Power BI can easily connect to the API endpoint to make information available for analysis.
Example API endpoint with parameters to retrieve all published data assets by data portal domain:

Austin, Texas

Discovery catalog endpoint: http://api.us.socrata.com/api/catalog/v1?search_context=data.austintexas.gov&published=true&limit=5000

Baton Rouge, Louisiana

Discovery catalog endpoint: http://api.us.socrata.com/api/catalog/v1?search_context=data.brla.gov&published=true&limit=5000

San Francisco, California

Discovery catalog endpoint: http://api.us.socrata.com/api/catalog/v1?search_context=data.sfgov.org&published=true&limit=5000


The following screenshot of a Power BI report demonstrates the type of useful information that can be found about the use of data assets from open data portals. The report and an excel file are available on the code repository for demonstration purposes.



Power BI Report of Discovery API Results




Data Portal Detailed Reports
Data portal publishers have additional analytic data available to them, including measures with date and time information and often share that information publicly.

title: About
text:
The toolkit identifies the types of measures that signal public use and engagement with open data and provides recommendations for regular reporting of actions and resulting activity.
The development of the open data actions and measures toolkit fulfills one part of a dissertation portfolio that focuses on measuring open data use and engagement to serve and empower the public. A review of open data research, public administration theory, and case studies of 3 local governments in the U.S. inform the recommendations.

title: Reporting
text: Reporting provides programs the opportunity to link actions to outcomes.

title: Reporting
text:
Annual Reporting
Open data policies can be a driver for reporting by including them as a requirement. For example the open data policy(Baton Rouge and Parish of East Baton Rouge, n.d.) for the City of Baton Rouge and Parish of East Baton Rouge requires on annual reporting that “includes an assessment of progress toward achievement of the goals of the City-Parish’s Open Data BR program (under which all City-Parish open data related activities occur), an assessment of how the City-Parish’s work has furthered or will further the City-Parish’s programmatic priorities, and a description and publication timeline for datasets envisioned to be published by the City-Parish in the following year”. Since 2018, they have published annual reports, including some reports published directly on one of their open data platforms.

Performance dashboards provide information about program priorities as well the results.

Web Analytics
The cumulative (lifetime) views, downloads, shares, embeds, and programmatic requests to datasets are provided by default by platforms on individual metadata pages and asset inventories. Programs may also track analytics on a daily basis to show use over time.
